To answer these questions, we review current cost allocation practices across different transmission planning regions to identify common trends and key differences in approaches. We use a selection of six case studies to identify drivers and contextual factors that influence project outcomes. This report focuses on the seven U.S. grid operators, either regional transmission organizations (RTOs) or independent system operators (ISOs). These RTOs and ISOs oversee delivery of two- thirds of electricity used in the country (FERC 2023). All but the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) are under FERC jurisdiction and therefore must comply with FERC’s transmission cost allocation requirements. The case studies are focused on projects identified through the RTO/ISO regional planning process rather than those developed through a local planning process or independently with negotiated, rather than regulated, service agreements. We do not consider cost allocation methods currently under development for compliance with FERC Order 1920. 6 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2 Current Trends in Transmission Cost Allocation and Investments ISOs and RTOs have used the discretion granted through FERC Order 1000 to develop a range of different transmission cost allocation methods. This section presents a summary of current cost allocation approaches and investment trends and identifies common themes and key differences among regions. 2.1 Taxonomy of Transmission Projects and Cost Allocation Methods One challenge with comparing cost allocation approaches across regions is that each region has a unique approach to characterize different types of projects and allocate costs. Across the seven ISOs/RTOs, there are nearly 20 different labels applied to transmission projects and more than a dozen different methods to allocate costs. To allow comparisons across regions and project types, we developed a cost allocation taxonomy whereby we group the transmission projects and cost allocation methods into six project types and five cost allocation approaches.
